ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.label: a rival in love
ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.summary: Two colonists are fond of the same person, and both of them know it. Walks, words between the rivals, and in the end a choice, made the game's own way or by the heart over time.

li.label: smitten
li.waiting: Next: a little time alone with {OTHER_nameDef}.

plain.li: I keep finding reasons to be wherever {OTHER_nameDef} is working. I've run out of good reasons and started using bad ones.
{OTHER_nameDef} laughed at something I said at supper. I've been thinking about it all day, which is ridiculous.
[night] Can't sleep. Thinking about {OTHER_nameDef}, which isn't helping.
Every time {OTHER_nameDef} walks into a room I forget what I came in for.

warm.li: I'd like to make {OTHER_nameDef}'s days a little easier. I'd like to be the reason {OTHER_pronoun} smiles. That's all, for now.

blunt.li: I like {OTHER_nameDef}. More than like. There, I've written it down.

cheerful.li: I made {OTHER_nameDef} laugh twice today! I'm keeping count, which I know is silly.

gloomy.li: Of course I've gone and fallen for {OTHER_nameDef}. Of course I have. Nothing good ever came of this.

cold.li: I find myself thinking about {OTHER_nameDef} at inconvenient times. I am treating it as a fact to be dealt with.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} has fallen for {OTHER_nameDef}, and everyone but {OTHER_nameDef} seems to know it.
{PAWN_nameDef} has been finding reasons to spend time with {OTHER_nameDef}.

li.label: a rival
li.waiting: Next: a word between {PAWN_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef}, who is fond of {OTHER_nameDef} too.

plain.li: {THIRD_nameDef} brought {OTHER_nameDef} a cup of something hot this morning. I saw {THIRD_objective} do it. I saw {OTHER_nameDef} smile.
I'm not the only one. {THIRD_nameDef} looks at {OTHER_nameDef} the way I do, and doesn't hide it as well as {THIRD_pronoun} thinks.
{THIRD_nameDef} and I keep turning up to help {OTHER_nameDef} with the same small jobs. It's getting embarrassing for all three of us.
[night] Lay awake listing everything {THIRD_nameDef} has that I don't. It was a long list and I didn't sleep.

warm.li: {THIRD_nameDef} is fond of {OTHER_nameDef} too, and {THIRD_nameDef} is a good person. That's the worst part.

blunt.li: {THIRD_nameDef} wants {OTHER_nameDef} too. Fine. Let {OTHER_nameDef} choose.

cheerful.li: So {THIRD_nameDef} has noticed {OTHER_nameDef} as well. Healthy competition! I'm going to be very charming.

gloomy.li: Of course there's someone else. {THIRD_nameDef}. I know how this goes, and it doesn't go my way.

cold.li: {THIRD_nameDef} is a rival for {OTHER_nameDef}'s affection. I will not do anything underhanded. I will be better than {THIRD_objective}.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} has eyes for {THIRD_nameDef} too. I'm not imagining it.
Every time I find a moment with {THIRD_nameDef}, {OTHER_nameDef} turns up with a basket that needs carrying.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} wants {THIRD_nameDef}. So do I. We'll see.

gloomy.li: I should have said something to {THIRD_nameDef} months ago. Now there's {OTHER_nameDef}.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} are both fond of {OTHER_nameDef}, and both of them know it.
There is a quiet rivalry in the colony: {PAWN_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef}, over {OTHER_nameDef}.

li.label: waiting for an answer
li.waiting: Next: {OTHER_nameDef} chooses one of them, or time and {OTHER_possessive} heart decide it.

plain.li: {THIRD_nameDef} and I had it out, quietly. We agreed it's {OTHER_nameDef}'s choice, not ours, and we'd both live with it. I hope I can.
Nothing to do now but wait and be myself, which is harder than it sounds.
I asked {OTHER_nameDef} to walk with me after supper, and {OTHER_pronoun} said yes, and then said nothing for a long time, and then said it was a nice evening.

warm.li: Whatever {OTHER_nameDef} decides, I want {OTHER_objective} to be happy. I keep saying that to myself until I mean it.

blunt.li: I've said my piece to {OTHER_nameDef}. Now I wait.

cheerful.li: I've told {OTHER_nameDef} how I feel, out loud! Now I can't sleep, but in a good way.

gloomy.li: I told {OTHER_nameDef}. I wish I hadn't. At least before, I didn't know.

cold.li: I have made my intentions clear to {OTHER_nameDef}. The decision is out of my hands.

plain.li: Two people in this colony are being very kind to me at once, and I know why, and I don't know what to do about it.
{OTHER_nameDef} asked me to walk with {OTHER_objective} tonight. So did {THIRD_nameDef}, yesterday. I need to think.

warm.li: Whoever I choose, someone gets hurt. I wish there were a kinder way to do this.

cheerful.li: I seem to be very popular this season! I'm flattered, and a little frightened.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I agreed to let {THIRD_nameDef} choose, and to shake hands on it either way. I meant it when I said it.

gloomy.li: We shook hands on it, {OTHER_nameDef} and I. I've a feeling I know whose hand I'll be shaking.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} have agreed to let {OTHER_nameDef} choose between them.
The colony is waiting to see whom {OTHER_nameDef} will choose: {PAWN_nameDef} or {THIRD_nameDef}.

plain.li: [won] {OTHER_nameDef} chose me. Me. I had to sit down. {THIRD_nameDef} shook my hand afterwards and meant it, which I'll remember.
[won] It's me {OTHER_nameDef} walks home with now. I keep checking it's true.
[lost] {OTHER_nameDef} chose {THIRD_nameDef}. I said all the right things. Then I went and split wood until my arms gave out.
[lost] I shook {THIRD_nameDef}'s hand, like we agreed. It was the hardest thing I've done this year.
[neither] {OTHER_nameDef} didn't choose either of us, in the end. {THIRD_nameDef} and I ended up drinking to that, which I didn't expect.
[neither] Nothing came of it, for me or for {THIRD_nameDef}. {OTHER_nameDef} is still {OTHER_nameDef}, and we're all still friends. Mostly.

warm.li: [won] {OTHER_nameDef} chose me, and I've promised myself to deserve it. I'll be gentle with {THIRD_nameDef} for a while.
[lost] {OTHER_nameDef} is happy with {THIRD_nameDef}. I can see it. I'm glad, and I'm sad, and I'll be all right.

blunt.li: [won] {OTHER_nameDef} picked me. Good.
[lost] {OTHER_nameDef} picked {THIRD_nameDef}. Fine. Leave me alone for a bit.
[neither] Neither of us got {OTHER_nameDef}. Waste of a season.

cheerful.li: [won] {OTHER_nameDef} said yes! I've been grinning all day and the others are sick of it.
[neither] Nobody won, so nobody lost! {THIRD_nameDef} and I are friends again, and that's something.

gloomy.li: [lost] I knew it would be {THIRD_nameDef}. I knew it the whole time and I hoped anyway.
[won] {OTHER_nameDef} chose me. I keep waiting for {OTHER_objective} to change {OTHER_possessive} mind.

cold.li: [lost] {OTHER_nameDef} chose {THIRD_nameDef}. I will be civil. It is the only thing left to do well.
[won] {OTHER_nameDef} chose me. I find I don't have a sensible thing to say about it.

plain.li: [won] I chose {OTHER_nameDef}. I think I knew for a while. Telling {THIRD_nameDef} was the hard part.
[lost] I chose {THIRD_nameDef}. {OTHER_nameDef} took it well, too well. I hope {OTHER_pronoun}'s all right.
[neither] I couldn't choose either of them, and I told them both so. It was a relief to stop pretending I might.
[won] {THIRD_nameDef} chose {OTHER_nameDef}. I shook {OTHER_possessive} hand, like we agreed. I'm going for a long walk.
[lost] {THIRD_nameDef} chose me. I keep catching myself smiling at nothing.
[neither] {THIRD_nameDef} chose neither of us. {OTHER_nameDef} and I got a little drunk about it, together.

chronicle.li: [won] {OTHER_nameDef} chose {PAWN_nameDef}, and {THIRD_nameDef} shook {PAWN_possessive} hand on it.
[lost] {OTHER_nameDef} chose {THIRD_nameDef}, and {PAWN_nameDef} kept {PAWN_possessive} word and wished them well.
[neither] In the end {OTHER_nameDef} chose neither {PAWN_nameDef} nor {THIRD_nameDef}, and the two rivals made their peace.

plain.li: [elsewhere] {OTHER_nameDef} has taken up with someone else altogether. {THIRD_nameDef} and I looked at each other across the table and nearly laughed.
[otherdead] {OTHER_nameDef} is dead. Whatever I hoped for, I never said it all.
[otherleft] {OTHER_nameDef} is gone from the colony. I never found out what {OTHER_pronoun} would have said.
[thirddead] {THIRD_nameDef} is dead. We wanted the same thing, and now I can't want it the same way.
[thirdleft] {THIRD_nameDef} has left the colony. It doesn't feel like winning.
[timeout] It's gone quiet, all of it. {OTHER_nameDef} is kind to both of us and promises nothing.
Whatever was between {OTHER_nameDef} and me has faded into an ordinary friendship. It might be for the best.

warm.li: [elsewhere] {OTHER_nameDef} has found someone, and it isn't either of us. I'm glad for {OTHER_objective}. I mean that.

blunt.li: [elsewhere] {OTHER_nameDef} picked someone else entirely. So much for that.

gloomy.li: [elsewhere] Neither of us, then. Someone else. Of course.

fizzleChronicle.li: [elsewhere] {OTHER_nameDef} took up with someone else, and the rivalry between {PAWN_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} came to nothing.
[thirddead] {THIRD_nameDef} died, and {PAWN_nameDef}'s rivalry with {THIRD_objective} died too.
The rivalry between {PAWN_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} over {OTHER_nameDef} has quietly ended.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} was fond of someone here, and never got to hear the answer. I hope it would have been yes.
{OTHER_nameDef} used to save the warm seat for someone. I keep seeing the empty seat.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} died with a question unanswered. There's nothing to be done about it now.

ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.label: torn between two students
ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.summary: A teacher with two students in the same craft, both wanting the teacher's eye. Jealousy, a fair word for each, the two of them making it up, and both coming on.

li.label: two at the bench
li.waiting: Next: a fair word for {OTHER_nameDef}, the first of the two students.

plain.li: Two students in {SKILL} now: {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef}. Two pairs of eyes on every move I make, and two sets of questions.
{OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} both want to be the one I praise. I've caught them watching which of them I look at first.
Teaching one student is a pleasure. Teaching two who are counting each other's compliments is a job.
[mentor] Two students at the same bench, both mine. I hadn't thought about how they'd feel about each other.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} both have it in them. I want to give each of them enough, and I'm not sure I have enough to give.

blunt.li: Two students. Both sulk when I help the other one. Grow up, the pair of you.

cheerful.li: Two students! The workshop is never quiet now. I'm loving it, mostly.

gloomy.li: Whichever of them I help, the other one notices. I'm going to get this wrong.

cold.li: Two students in {SKILL}. Their rivalry could be useful if it's managed. I intend to manage it.

plain.li: I'm not {OTHER_nameDef}'s only student any more. {THIRD_nameDef} is at the bench every day now, asking the same questions I asked.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} spent the whole morning with {THIRD_nameDef}. I didn't say anything. I wanted to.

plain.li: {THIRD_nameDef} was here first, and never lets me forget it. I'll learn faster, that's all.

blunt.li: {THIRD_nameDef} is good. I'll be better.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} is teaching two students in {SKILL}, {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef}, and they both want {PAWN_possessive} eye.
{OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} are learning {SKILL} side by side from {PAWN_nameDef}, and keeping score.

li.label: a fair word for each
li.waiting: Next: a fair word for {THIRD_nameDef}, the second student.

plain.li: Sat down with {OTHER_nameDef} and went over everything, honestly. Now I owe {THIRD_nameDef} the same.
{OTHER_nameDef} asked me straight whether I liked {THIRD_nameDef}'s work better. I said they're good at different things. It's true.

warm.li: I told {OTHER_nameDef} what {OTHER_pronoun} does better than anyone. Tomorrow I'll find the words for {THIRD_nameDef}.

blunt.li: Had it out with {OTHER_nameDef}. {THIRD_nameDef}'s turn next.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} looked so relieved when I explained it. One down, one to go!

gloomy.li: I fixed things with {OTHER_nameDef}, I think. Which means {THIRD_nameDef} will feel left out now.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} has been told plainly where {OTHER_pronoun} stands. {THIRD_nameDef} is owed the same courtesy.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} sat down with {OTHER_nameDef} and was honest about {OTHER_possessive} work, and {THIRD_nameDef}'s.

li.label: at the same bench
li.waiting: Next: {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} making it up between themselves, or a few days without a sharp word.

plain.li: Both of them have heard it from me now: they're good at different things, and I'm not choosing. The rest is up to the two of them.
I've stopped refereeing. {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} will have to sort it out at the bench, like I did with mine.

warm.li: I'd like those two to be friends. They'd be good for each other. I'll leave the door open and see.

blunt.li: Told them both. Now they can sort it out themselves.

cheerful.li: I caught {OTHER_nameDef} lending {THIRD_nameDef} a tool today. Without being asked!

gloomy.li: They're still keeping score. Maybe they always will.

cold.li: I have done what a teacher can. The students' relationship is theirs to settle.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} says {THIRD_nameDef} and I are good at different things. I've started to see what {OTHER_pronoun} means.
{THIRD_nameDef} told me I have a better eye than {OTHER_nameDef}. Then told me {OTHER_nameDef} has a steadier hand. I'm not sure that was a compliment.

chronicle.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef}, {PAWN_nameDef}'s two students, are learning to share the bench.

li.label: both coming on
li.waiting: Next: work in {SKILL} from both {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef}.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} have started checking each other's work before they bring it to me. I've got less to correct and more to teach.
The two of them are working side by side now, arguing about technique instead of about me. It's a joy to listen to.

warm.li: They're helping each other now. I didn't make that happen. I just got out of the way.

blunt.li: They've stopped squabbling and started working. About time.

cheerful.li: My two students are a team now! A noisy, opinionated team.

gloomy.li: They get on now. I keep waiting for it to fall apart. It hasn't.

cold.li: The rivalry has become a collaboration. Their output has improved accordingly.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef}'s two students, {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef}, have stopped competing and started helping each other.

plain.li: [otherahead] {OTHER_nameDef} has pulled ahead in {SKILL} this season, and {THIRD_nameDef} was the first to say so. I'm proud of both of them for different reasons.
[thirdahead] {THIRD_nameDef} came on furthest this season, and {OTHER_nameDef} helped {THIRD_objective} do it. That's the part I'll remember.
[even] Neither of them is ahead. They've come on together, step for step, and they know it.
I've had two students in {SKILL} and never had to choose between them. That was the whole trick: not choosing.

warm.li: Two students, both standing on their own feet, both friends. I couldn't ask for more.

blunt.li: Both of them are good now. My work's mostly done.

cheerful.li: Both my students are doing brilliantly, and they get on! Best season at the bench I've had.

gloomy.li: They don't need me as much now, either of them. That's the point. It still stings a little.

cold.li: Both students have reached a satisfactory standard. Neither was neglected. I count it a success.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} says {THIRD_nameDef} and I are both coming on well. I believe {OTHER_objective}. I've watched {THIRD_nameDef} work.
I used to count every word {THIRD_nameDef} gave {OTHER_nameDef}. I've stopped. We're both better for having the other at the bench.

chronicle.li: [otherahead] {OTHER_nameDef} has come on furthest of {PAWN_nameDef}'s two students, with {THIRD_nameDef}'s help.
[thirdahead] {THIRD_nameDef} has come on furthest of {PAWN_nameDef}'s two students, with {OTHER_nameDef}'s help.
{PAWN_nameDef}'s two students in {SKILL} have both come into their own, and become friends along the way.

plain.li: [fight] {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} came to blows at the bench today. I've failed them both, somewhere.
[otherdead] {OTHER_nameDef} is dead. {THIRD_nameDef} works alone at the bench now, and so quietly.
[thirddead] {THIRD_nameDef} is dead. {OTHER_nameDef} keeps setting out two of everything.
[otherleft] {OTHER_nameDef} has left the colony, and with {OTHER_objective} half of what I was teaching.
[thirdleft] {THIRD_nameDef} has gone. {OTHER_nameDef} has the bench to {OTHER_objective}self and doesn't seem to want it.
[timeout] They still keep score, those two. I've stopped trying to make them stop.
I taught them both, as fairly as I could. Whatever is between them, it's theirs now.

gloomy.li: [fight] My two students hate each other, and they learned it at my bench.

blunt.li: [fight] They fought. Both of them out of the workshop for a week.

fizzleChronicle.li: [fight] {PAWN_nameDef}'s two students, {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef}, came to blows, and the lessons stopped.
{PAWN_nameDef}'s two students never quite stopped competing.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} taught two of us at once, and never let either of us feel second. I don't know how {OTHER_pronoun} did it.
{OTHER_nameDef} left two students behind. We'll keep the bench going between us.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef}'s teaching was unfinished. The students will have to finish it themselves.

ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.label: brothers and sisters
ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.summary: Two brothers or sisters at odds, and the parent between them: a word with each, an uneasy peace, and in time a family that can sit at one table.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} are at it again. You'd think two people who came from the same place could share a room.
I found {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} not speaking at supper, and both of them looking at me to take a side.
[young] My two have been squabbling since breakfast. Over a stick. It's always a stick.
[grown] My children are grown and they still fight like they did when they were small. Only quieter, which is worse.

warm.li: I love both of them. I wish they could see in each other what I see in them.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} need their heads knocked together. Figuratively.

cheerful.li: My two are bickering again. I suppose it means they care what the other thinks!

gloomy.li: My children can't stand each other. I must have done something wrong, long ago.

cold.li: The friction between my children is affecting the household. It needs addressing.

plain.li: {THIRD_nameDef} started it. {THIRD_nameDef} always starts it, and {OTHER_nameDef} always takes {THIRD_possessive} side.

blunt.li: I'm not apologizing to {THIRD_nameDef}. Not first.

plain.li: {THIRD_nameDef} gets away with everything. {OTHER_nameDef} never sees it.

chronicle.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} have been at odds, and their parent {PAWN_nameDef} is caught between them.
The quarrel between {PAWN_nameDef}'s children, {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef}, is wearing on everyone.

plain.li: Had it out with {OTHER_nameDef}, gently. We both cried a little, then laughed. Now {THIRD_nameDef}.
{OTHER_nameDef} told me {OTHER_possessive} side of it. It's not the side I'd heard. There's always another side.
[young] Sat {OTHER_nameDef} on my knee and asked what was really wrong. It wasn't the stick.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} just wanted to be heard. I can do that much. {THIRD_nameDef} deserves the same.

blunt.li: Talked to {OTHER_nameDef}. Now {THIRD_nameDef}. Then they talk to each other.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and I had a lovely long talk! I think I understand {OTHER_objective} better now.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} said I always take {THIRD_nameDef}'s side. Maybe I do.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef}'s grievances have been heard. {THIRD_nameDef}'s are next.

plain.li: Talked with {OTHER_nameDef} today. Properly. I didn't know {OTHER_pronoun} worried about us that much.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} sat down with {OTHER_nameDef} and heard {OTHER_possessive} side of the family quarrel.

li.label: an uneasy peace
li.waiting: Next: a few days with no sharp words between {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef}.

plain.li: I've heard them both out. Now I'm watching, and holding my breath, and not saying anything.
{OTHER_nameDef} passed {THIRD_nameDef} the salt at supper without being asked. I nearly dropped my spoon.
[young] Two whole days without a fight over the stick. I've hidden the stick.

warm.li: They're trying, both of them. I can see it. I'm so proud I could burst.

blunt.li: Quiet in the house. Long may it last.

cheerful.li: No shouting today, and not a single door slammed!

gloomy.li: It's quiet, for now. It never lasts.

cold.li: A truce of sorts has been observed. I am monitoring it.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} sat me down and listened to all of it. I said things I've never said. I think {OTHER_pronoun} understands now.

chronicle.li: An uneasy peace holds between {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef}.

li.label: one table
li.waiting: Next: {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} thinking a little better of each other, or a talk of their own.

plain.li: Three days and not a cross word between them. I don't trust it yet. I want to.
I heard {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} laughing together in the yard. I stayed out of sight so as not to spoil it.

warm.li: My two are finding their way back to each other. I mustn't hurry them.

blunt.li: Still quiet. Good.

cheerful.li: They're laughing together again! I'd forgotten what that sounds like.

gloomy.li: Still no fighting. I keep waiting for it to start again.

cold.li: The peace is holding. Now it needs to become something more than the absence of quarrels.

chronicle.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} have gone days without quarrelling, and {PAWN_nameDef} is starting to hope.

plain.li: All three of us at one table tonight, and nobody left it angry. It's a small thing. It isn't small to me.
{OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} went off to work together this morning, arguing about something, the friendly way.
[young] My two built something together in the yard. I'm not allowed to see it yet. They're allies now, against me.
[grown] My children are friends again. They'll outlive me, and they'll have each other. That was what I wanted.

warm.li: My family is whole again. I didn't fix it. They did. I just held the door open.

blunt.li: Family's back together. Took long enough.

cheerful.li: We had supper together, the three of us, and it was loud and silly and wonderful.

gloomy.li: They're getting on now. I'll treasure it while it lasts.

cold.li: The household is at peace. I consider it the most important work I have done this year.

plain.li: {THIRD_nameDef} and I worked the whole morning together and it was fine. Better than fine. Don't tell {OTHER_nameDef}, {OTHER_pronoun}'ll cry.
{THIRD_nameDef} isn't so bad. I've told {OTHER_nameDef} so. Once is enough.

chronicle.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} have made their peace, and {PAWN_nameDef}'s family sits at one table again.
{PAWN_nameDef}'s children are friends again.

plain.li: [fight] {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} came to blows. My own children. I sat in the dark a long time afterwards.
[otherdead] {OTHER_nameDef} is dead, and {THIRD_nameDef} never made it up with {OTHER_objective}. Neither of us can bear to talk about it.
[thirddead] {THIRD_nameDef} is gone, and the last words between my children were angry ones.
[otherleft] {OTHER_nameDef} has left the colony. The quarrel went with {OTHER_objective}, unfinished.
[thirdleft] {THIRD_nameDef} has left. I don't know if they'll ever make it up now.
[timeout] I've tried and tried. My children still can't stand each other, and I'm out of words.
My two still aren't friends. Perhaps they'll come to it on their own, when I'm not looking.

warm.li: [timeout] They're not ready yet. I'll keep loving them both until they are.

blunt.li: [timeout] Gave up trying to make them get on. Their problem now.

gloomy.li: [timeout] My family is broken and I can't mend it.

fizzleChronicle.li: [fight] {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} came to blows, and {PAWN_nameDef}'s hopes of peace in the family went with it.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} spent the last of {OTHER_possessive} days trying to make peace between {OTHER_possessive} children. We owe it to {OTHER_objective} to finish it.
{OTHER_nameDef} just wanted the family at one table. We'll set {OTHER_possessive} place.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} died with the family still divided. That is a debt the rest of us now carry.

ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.label: caught in the middle
ColonyCouncil.ArcDef.summary: Two friends have fallen out, and the colonist is the one both of them talk to. A word with each, then the two of them under one roof, and maybe the three of them friends again.

li.label: between two friends
li.waiting: Next: a talk with {OTHER_nameDef} about the falling-out.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} have fallen out, and somehow I'm the one both of them come to with it.
{OTHER_nameDef} wants me to agree {THIRD_nameDef} is impossible. {THIRD_nameDef} wants me to agree about {OTHER_nameDef}. I agree with nobody and get glared at by both.
Ate supper between {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} tonight. Neither of them spoke to the other. I spoke to both, alternately, like a ferry.

warm.li: I love them both. I won't choose, and I won't let them make me.

blunt.li: My two friends hate each other now. Wonderful.

cheerful.li: I'm the colony's official go-between now! The pay is terrible.

gloomy.li: Whatever I say to one of them, the other hears about it and holds it against me.

cold.li: Two of my friends are in conflict. I am being used as an intermediary. I will set terms.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} is the only one who understands what {THIRD_nameDef} did. At least I hope {OTHER_pronoun} does.
I hope {OTHER_nameDef} isn't listening to {THIRD_nameDef}'s version. {OTHER_nameDef} is my friend too.

chronicle.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} have fallen out, and {PAWN_nameDef}, a friend to both, is caught in the middle.

plain.li: Heard {OTHER_nameDef}'s side, all of it. It sounds reasonable from where {OTHER_pronoun} stands. I expect {THIRD_nameDef}'s will too.
{OTHER_nameDef} asked me not to tell {THIRD_nameDef} what {OTHER_pronoun} said. I won't. I'll tell {THIRD_nameDef} that {OTHER_nameDef} misses {THIRD_objective}, which is also true.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} doesn't hate {THIRD_nameDef}, only hurts. Those are different things.

blunt.li: Got {OTHER_nameDef}'s side. Now {THIRD_nameDef}'s. Then I'm done carrying messages.

cheerful.li: Half the peace treaty is drafted! The other half is {THIRD_nameDef}.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} talked for an hour. I feel like I carried it all home with me.

cold.li: One party's grievances recorded. The other's are next.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} heard {OTHER_nameDef}'s side of the quarrel with {THIRD_nameDef}.

li.label: under one roof
li.waiting: Next: {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} talking it out between themselves, or a few days of getting along.

plain.li: I've heard both of them out, and told each what the other wouldn't say. Now I've stepped back. They'll have to do the rest.
Told {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef}, both at once, that I'm done carrying messages. They looked at me, then at each other.

warm.li: I've done what a friend can. The rest is theirs. I hope they find their way.

blunt.li: No more messages. They can talk to each other.

cheerful.li: I've retired as go-between! Now we wait and see.

gloomy.li: I've stepped back. If it falls apart now, at least it won't be in my hands.

cold.li: I have withdrawn from mediation. The outcome depends on them.

plain.li: {THIRD_nameDef} says {OTHER_nameDef} misses me. I don't know whether to believe it. I want to.

chronicle.li: {PAWN_nameDef} has stepped back, and left {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} to settle it themselves.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} sat down together at supper tonight, and kept a seat for me between them. Not as a buffer. As a friend.
I'm out of the middle. {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} talk to each other now, not through me, and I can just be friends with both.
The three of us laughed about the whole thing tonight. I'm not sure it was funny. It was good to laugh.

warm.li: My friends are friends again. I'd almost forgotten how easy things are when nobody's keeping score.

blunt.li: They made up. I'm off duty.

cheerful.li: Peace in our time! The three of us had supper together and nobody stormed off.

gloomy.li: They've made up. I'm relieved. I'm also tired in a way I didn't know I could be.

cold.li: The conflict is resolved. My time is my own again.

plain.li: {THIRD_nameDef} and I have made up. {OTHER_nameDef} stood between us the whole time and never once took a side. I owe {OTHER_objective}.
{THIRD_nameDef} and I are friends again. {OTHER_nameDef} carried both our tempers for weeks. We bought {OTHER_objective} a drink.

chronicle.li: {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} have made up, and {PAWN_nameDef} is out of the middle at last.

plain.li: [fight] {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} came to blows today. I was standing right there. I couldn't stop it.
[otherdead] {OTHER_nameDef} is dead, and {THIRD_nameDef} never got to say sorry. Now I carry it for both of them.
[thirddead] {THIRD_nameDef} is dead. {OTHER_nameDef} won't talk about it, and I don't know what to say.
[otherleft] {OTHER_nameDef} has left the colony, quarrel and all.
[thirdleft] {THIRD_nameDef} has gone, and the quarrel went unfinished.
[timeout] They still won't speak. I've stopped trying to make them. I'm just tired.
My two friends are still at odds. I've given up being the bridge.

warm.li: [timeout] I'll go on being a friend to both of them. That's all I can do.

blunt.li: [timeout] Still not speaking. Not my problem any more.

fizzleChronicle.li: [fight] {OTHER_nameDef} and {THIRD_nameDef} came to blows, and {PAWN_nameDef}'s efforts to make peace between them came to nothing.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} spent weeks carrying messages between two people who wouldn't speak. One of them was me. I'm sorry, {OTHER_nameDef}.
{OTHER_nameDef} never once took a side. I didn't understand what that cost until now.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} was a fair go-between. The colony is shorter one of those now.
